# IN QUEER STREET — Fergus Hume (compact notes)

Source: Gutenberg #56087. F.V. White & Co., London, 1913. 21 chapters. Single book.

## Contents
I Boarding-House; II Old School-Fellows; III Man Proposes; IV Advertisement; V Next Step; VI Seeking Trouble; VII Amazing Discovery; VIII Family History; IX Gwen; X Vane's Aunt; XI Macbeth's Banquet; XII Cupid's Garden; XIII Danger; XIV At Bay; XV A Friend in Need; XVI Explanations; XVII Blackmail; XVIII Hench's Diplomacy; XIX A Denial; XX Reaping the Whirlwind; XXI The Sunshine of Life.

## Characters
- **Cuthbert Spruce** ("the Nut", "Cherub", "little Spruce"): pink/white cherubic, dandy, cheat, expelled from West End for cheating at cards. Educated Winchester & Cambridge. Dislikes work. Calls himself a novelist researching Bethnal Green. Ultimately blackmailer and murderer.
- **Mrs. Tesk**: ex-schoolmistress, landlady of "The Home of the Muses" (boarding house, Bethnal Green; 25s/week). Pedantic, prim. Servants: Amelia (16, maid-of-all-work), cook, Simon Jedd "Bottles".
- **Madame Alpenny**: Hungarian-born, married Englishman, stout, sallow, red hair, orange-spotted dark dress, black velvet bead mantle, large floppy picture-hat, jewellery; gambler; father a diplomatist; once met Hench's father in Buda Pesth ~20 years earlier, refused his marriage offer; scheming, wants rich son-in-law.
- **Zara Alpenny**: her daughter, dancer at Bijou Music-hall (Fire-dance), tall, gaunt, gipsy-like, dark eyes; loves Edward "Ned" Bracken; later marries him at a Registrar's office.
- **Edward "Ned" Bracken**: second violin, Bijou orchestra; rough, unkempt; mother dying at Folkestone.
- **Owain Hench** (born Owain Evans; "Hench" = father's assumed name): tall, brown hair, brown eyes, spade beard (shaved later), 25 on 10 July; Winchester; travelled with spendthrift father (died Paris, buried Père Lachaise); worked as writer/sailor. Ankle injured by motor-car saving Gwen.
- **Simon Jedd "Bottles"**: 15, freckled, red-haired, snub nose, hero-worships Hench; detective-story reader; mother Mrs. Jedd, wardrobe mistress at Bijou. Twin brother **Peter Jedd**, page at Mrs. Perage's.
- **James (Jim) Vane**: barrister, Chancery Lane chambers, thirty, thin dark hair greying, hatchet face; Hench's Winchester friend; aunt Mrs. Emma Perage.
- **Mrs. Emma Perage**: Vane's aunt, Cookley; tall, gaunt, masculine-looking, contralto, rubs her nose; widow, childless; manages estates; matchmaker.
- **Gwen Evans**: Madoc's daughter, ~20, small, slender, blue eyes, golden hair; £500/yr own income; father cruel.
- **Squire Madoc Evans**: Cookley Grange; murdered in Parley Wood near Gipsy Stile by carving-knife with horn handle, ~7:30 pm, 1 July; unpopular, hard on poachers.
- **Mynydd Evans** (grandfather, "Great Evans"): Welsh, Rhaiadr (waterfall) in South Wales; London merchant; bought Cookley Grange; left ~£11,000/yr; Madoc got it, Owain's father cut off (£500–600/yr allowance).
- **Owain Evans senior** (Hench's father): elder son, cut off; married English governess (Hench's mother, died early); gambler; spendthrift; died Paris ~5 yrs before.
- **Mr. Samuel Gilberry** (senior partner, Gilberry & Gilberry, solicitors, Lincoln's Inn Fields): snuff, white beard, Father Christmas look.
- **Mrs. Bell**: delicate landlady, Cookley cottage; nephew **Giles** (labourer).
- **Mrs. Capes**: Grange housekeeper; recognized Hench as Owain's son.
- **Betsy Jane**: barmaid at Bull Inn who spoke with tramp.

## Timeline
1. Spruce arrives at Mrs. Tesk's (late June); meets Hench (eight years since Winchester; Hench "Owen"/"Owain" spelling). Spruce wins Madame's jewellery at cards.
2. Hench returns (Sunday). Papers at Gilberry's due at 25th birthday (10 July). Madame recalls Hench's father (Owain of Rhaiadr). Hench proposes to Zara; she refuses ("you want a home, not love"); she loves Bracken.
3. Advertisement in *The Express*: "If Rhaiadr will come to the Gipsy Stile, Cookley, Essex, at eight o'clock on the 1st of July…" Madame shows it. Spruce leaves; Bottles borrows 5s, goes to brother; gives Hench's address? (Bottles tells Madame later via Peter).
4. Hench goes to Bloomsbury hotel (Burney Street), then Cookley 1 July; sees tramp-like Madame-type figure at station (thinks it is Madame). Kills nothing; finds Squire Evans dead near Gipsy Stile; flees on foot ~30 miles to London.
5. Hench shaves beard at Brampton Road barber; takes rooms South Kensington. Vane helps, gives tailor's makeover. Inquest verdict "wilful murder against persons unknown". 10 July: Gilberry reveals Hench is Owain Evans, heir to ~£10,000/yr; Madoc was his uncle.
6. Hench goes to Cookley as "Mr. Hench", rents Mrs. Bell's rooms. Rescues Gwen from motor-car on the bend near church; ankle hurt. Gwen: "My name is Evans."
7. Mrs. Perage dinner (Chapter XI); Gwen asks Hench to find murderer; Gwen mentions woman in orange-spotted dress visited Madoc (June); Hench lies "gipsies".
8. Garden kiss; Gwen says she'll marry him after he finds the killer. Gwen suspected by villagers.
9. Vane visits; Hench confesses to Vane and then Gwen (churchyard, Saxon Cross). Madame Alpenny appears, accuses Hench; Gwen learns Hench proposed to Zara; flees. Madame gives "one week".
10. Mrs. Perage hears all; Zara and Bracken come to Cookley; Zara explains to Gwen; reconciliation.
11. Spruce visits Hench at Mrs. Bell's, blackmails for £2,000/yr. Gives week.
12. Next morning Vane and Hench plan; Spruce returns to Bull Inn; Peter and Simon's telegram revealed: Simon followed Madame (1 July) and Spruce in disguise (orange-spotted dress, red wig, bead mantle, hat borrowed from Mrs. Jedd).
13. Hench to London: Zara and Bracken have married (Registrar). Mrs. Tesk dismissed Bottles for theft of horn-handled carving-knife (Spruce took it from Mrs. Tesk's table). Hench confronts Madame; she denies, claims Hampstead Ponds appointment (anonymous letter, 6–10 pm, 1 July, torn up).
14. Bull Inn (Chapter XX), Hench, Vane, Simon testify; Spruce confesses, flees over garden wall to churchyard/Parley Wood; sets fire; trapped by falling tree and crushed; dies. Parley Wood burns. Hench faints; Vane catches him.
15. Chapter XXI: Spruce buried at Cookley. Hench recovers at Mrs. Perage's (nine days). Plans: marry Gwen in three weeks, year abroad. Bottles to school; mother's income; Peter rewarded. Zara & Bracken to America; Madame to Hungary, gambling; Hench gives Bracken £1,000 (refused by Bracken, then accepted per chance). Final line: "here begins the new life!" Owain rises with Gwen's arm.

## Key quotes
- Spruce's line: "Queer Street, which, like Bohemia, is nowhere and yet is everywhere."
- Mrs. Perage: "Fudge!"; "Hum!"
- Hench: "Owain of Rhaiadr"; Rhaiadr means waterfall.
- Gilberry: "ten thousand a year."
- Ending: "And here begins the new life!" — Owain.
